title: HINT for Marketing — copy stays on-brand and proven
metaDescription: Keep brand voice, terminology, channel limits and claim proof beside campaigns so assistants write on-brand copy without unsupported promises.
h1: Your assistant writes copy fast. HINT keeps it on-brand and supportable.
intro: HINT keeps voice, approved terms, channel limits and proof rules in plain-text notes beside each brand's work. Your assistant reads the rules for this client and campaign before drafting copy.

situations.before: A slogan sounds right but violates a banned-term rule.
situations.after: Brand language travels with the campaign
situations.body: Preferred and prohibited wording appears before copy is drafted, not only during final review.

situations.before: The copy calls a product the best without substantiation.
situations.after: Claims carry proof or a flag
situations.body: The assistant links support, adds the required disclaimer, or marks the sentence for legal review.

situations.before: One client's voice leaks into another client's campaign.
situations.body: Agency-wide policy can be shared while brand voice and assets stay inside the client folder.

example.intro: The Sterling Cooper demo grounds Acme's spring campaign in an approved source.
example.after: It writes inside Acme's voice and channel limits, then identifies every statement that still needs proof or approval.
example.compiled:
<campaign name="acme-1">
  Approved campaign grounded in SRC-1.
</campaign>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: State an unsubstantiated product or performance claim.
Use banned terms or disparage a competitor.
Apply one brand's voice, assets or claims to another brand.
disclaimer: HINT keeps brand and claim rules visible; marketing, legal and regulatory reviewers retain approval responsibility.

faq.q: Does this make copy less creative?
faq.a: No. It defines the brand and compliance boundaries; the assistant can explore freely inside them.

faq.q: Can an agency manage multiple brands?
faq.a: Yes. Shared agency rules live above client folders, while each brand's voice and assets remain isolated.
No. It identifies the declared disclaimer or review requirement and flags missing proof for the authorized reviewer.

keywordDescriptions.brand: Defines positioning and the identity whose rules apply.
keywordDescriptions.audience: Names a declared segment for the message.
keywordDescriptions.term: Records preferred language and disallowed variants.
keywordDescriptions.banned: Lists wording that must not appear.
keywordDescriptions.campaign: Defines a campaign's goal, audience and period.
keywordDescriptions.message: States a campaign message for a named audience.
keywordDescriptions.claim: States a marketing assertion that requires support or review.
keywordDescriptions.proof: Identifies evidence that substantiates a claim.
keywordDescriptions.channel: Sets format, length and disclaimer constraints.
